picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236, RAS(ON) multi-selective)
picks.rationale: This is the one option here with a real ORR number in real 2L PDAC: 35% response, 8.5-month PFS, 13.1-month OS at 300 mg (n=26) — roughly double what NALIRIFOX or gem/nab buy in this setting. G12R sits inside the pooled G12 cohort, and the preclinical work (PMID 38589574, 38593348) shows G12R lines regress in the same exposure window as G12D, so I am comfortable extrapolating. The upside I am chasing: a durable RECIST response from an oral drug, with a registrational phase 3 already running — about as close to a sure thing as advanced G12R PDAC offers. Recruiting on NCT05379985 and the chemo-combo NCT06445062, so it is actually reachable.
primary_concerns: The 35% ORR is a pooled G12 estimate; a G12R-only response rate has never been published, and Singhi 2025 argues G12R runs lower ERK flux, which cuts both ways
Class toxicity is near-universal — 96% any-grade, 30% grade 3+, with the EGFR-type rash and GI toxicity that come with pan-RAS blockade
RASolute 302 is active-not-recruiting, so daraxonrasib access may hinge on an expanded-access route rather than an open slot

picks.intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 (pan-RAS molecular glue)
picks.rationale: The early signal is loud: PDAC unconfirmed ORR 40-42% and 14 of 14 KRAS G12X patients with 75%+ ctDNA drops, five reaching full clearance, no DLTs through cutoff. If even part of that holds on confirmation this is a best-in-class response rate for the disease, and deep ctDNA clearance is the kind of molecular-response signal I weight heavily. I will say plainly this is a phase-1 press release, not a paper — grade-3 rates and confirmed responses are not public yet. But a treat-to-remission patient who accepts high-risk-high-reward is exactly who this bet is for, and NCT06895031 is recruiting.
primary_concerns: Evidence is a single April 2026 topline release — no peer review, no confirmed ORR, no per-term grade-3+ safety, so the 40-42% could shrink on confirmation
G12R is not broken out separately; the ctDNA and response data are pooled across G12X
First-in-class molecular glue means the long-tail toxicity and durability picture is genuinely unknown

picks.intervention_label: ulixertinib (ERK1/2i) + palbociclib (CDK4/6i)
picks.rationale: This is the only option that hits three of the patient's drivers at once — ERK downstream of KRAS G12R plus the CDK4/6 dependency created by CDKN2A loss and the CCND3 alteration. The preclinical synergy is not hand-waving: six of six PDAC organoids showed cooperative kill and xenograft regression where either single agent only stalled growth (PMID 36346366). The upside scenario is that vertical MAPK-plus-cell-cycle blockade holds where monotherapy CDK4/6 flops, and the PDAC expansion on NCT03454035 takes patients by histology, so G12R is no barrier to entry. Thin clinical evidence, but the mechanistic case is the strongest multi-feature fit on the board.
primary_concerns: No PDAC efficacy readout yet — this rides almost entirely on organoid and xenograft synergy, and single-agent palbociclib already failed in CDK4/6-amplified baskets (ORR 4%, PMID 39437014)
Overlapping toxicity: MEK/ERK rash and diarrhea stacked on CDK4/6 neutropenia may force dose compromises that erode the synergy
The synergy models are mostly G12D/G12V organoids; G12R's lower ERK flux is an untested variable

picks.intervention_label: KST-6051 / FALCON (pan-KRAS ON/OFF inhibitor)
picks.rationale: A pan-KRAS Switch-II binder covering both ON and OFF states that names PDAC as a target tumor, so a G12R patient qualifies on the KRAS-mutation gate alone. The reason to hold a slot here is mechanistic optionality: if the RAS(ON) agents hit resistance or a rash the patient cannot tolerate, an ON/OFF-active pan-KRAS drug is a distinct shot at the same dependency. No efficacy exists yet — first patient dosed April 2026 — so this is a forward-looking placeholder, not a data-backed pick. JAB-23E73 (NCT06959615) is the near-identical fallback if FALCON has no open slot.
primary_concerns: Zero clinical efficacy or safety data — this is a phase-1 dose-escalation that opened this year
Early cohorts mean limited slots and a real chance of sub-therapeutic starting doses
No G12R-specific data; eligibility rests on the broad KRAS-mutation gate rather than demonstrated allele activity

picks.intervention_label: ELI-002 (amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine, G12R-encoded)
picks.rationale: The vaccine directly encodes the G12R neoantigen, and the AMPLIFY-201 data are genuinely provocative — 84% T-cell response, with high responders reaching RFS and OS not-reached versus 3-16 months in low responders (PMID 40790272, 38195752). The catch I will not hide: all of that is in MRD-positive resected disease, and this patient is overtly recurrent, which sits outside the enrollment window and is a harder setting for a vaccine to control bulk tumor. I rank it because the mechanism-fit for the exact allele is clean, and an immune-directed route is one of the few things that could produce durable control in MSS disease where checkpoint monotherapy is dead. Low confidence, and I would only reach for it via a recurrent-setting protocol or the mKRASvax-plus-dual-checkpoint route.
primary_concerns: All human data are in the MRD-positive adjuvant window; there is no evidence a vaccine controls overt bulk recurrent PDAC
The registered ELI-002 7P cohort is active-not-recruiting and enrolls resected MRD patients, so this patient likely does not fit without a different protocol
T-cell response, not tumor shrinkage, is the primary readout — immunogenicity has not been shown to translate into RECIST response in this disease

notes: Ranked around the pan-RAS / pan-KRAS axis because G12R is GTP-loaded and outside the covalent G12C window (Hobbs PMID 31649109) — sotorasib/adagrasib are off-axis regardless of their PDAC ORRs. Daraxonrasib is the load-bearing pick: the only real ORR in real 2L PDAC with G12R in scope. ERAS-0015 outranks the naked pan-KRAS phase-1s because it actually has a PDAC efficacy signal, thin as the press-release evidence is. Ulixertinib+palbociclib is my multi-feature swing — the only option touching KRAS, CDKN2A and CCND3 together. Left off MTAP/PRMT5 (gated on unconfirmed MTAP co-deletion) and the olaparib/PARP axis (gated on absent germline data plus no platinum exposure) — both contingent, not actionable today. Patient has no toxicity vetoes and an explicit high-risk-high-reward, treat-to-remission preference, which is why I lead with the striking-signal options rather than hedging toward chemo.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985
picks.rationale: Still the best-characterized safety profile of any G12R-active option here, and the re-run does not change that. The NEJM 2026 pivotal cohort dosed 168 PDAC patients: any-grade TRAE 96%, G3+ 30%, with the AE picture fully mapped — rash 91% any-grade / 8% G3+, diarrhea 48% / 2% G3+, stomatitis 31% / 3%, nausea 43%, fatigue 20%. These are skin and GI events with routine management algorithms borrowed from the EGFR-inhibitor playbook: topical steroids plus low-dose doxycycline for the rash, a loperamide ladder for diarrhea, dexamethasone mouthwash for stomatitis. The 2L RAS G12 subgroup at 300 mg reached ORR 35%, mPFS 8.5 mo, mOS 13.1 mo (n=26), and G12R sits inside that pooled estimand. No organ-failure signals across the 168-patient denominator and no DLT-class surprises through dose-escalation. Against a re-run field that now includes three pan-KRAS/pan-RAS agents with no published AE-grade distribution, this is the one pan-RAS option whose toxicity I can actually manage from a written algorithm.
primary_concerns: G12R-specific subgroup ORR is not broken out from the pooled G12X estimand — the 35% is allele-pooled
Longest-followed patients sit at roughly 2 years; the conservative-default 5-year safety threshold is not met for the pan-RAS class
Rash and stomatitis management adds visit burden but is not dose-limiting at 300 mg

picks.intervention_label: olaparib 300 mg PO BID maintenance after platinum induction — contingent on germline BRCA1/2 result
picks.rationale: The most mature safety dataset in the candidate set, and the re-run adds nothing that competes on that axis. POLO is a RoB2-low phase 3 RCT, FDA-approved since 2019, with 7 years of post-marketing surveillance in PDAC on top of a deeper PARP-class record from the ovarian and breast labels. G3+ AEs 40% on olaparib vs 23% on placebo, AE-driven discontinuation 5%, no fatal events in the registrational arm. The class AEs — anemia, fatigue, nausea, and an MDS/AML risk of roughly 1.5% on prolonged exposure — all have NCCN-published management algorithms. Two hard gates remain: the germline BRCA1/2 / PALB2 panel is not on file (target_validation row germline-pdac-hboc-lynch-lfs-panel is the workup), and the patient has had zero platinum exposure since adjuvant FOLFIRI was irinotecan-only. POLO entry requires at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum without progression. Both gates are load-bearing: no germline hit and no platinum induction means this pathway is not operative.
primary_concerns: Germline BRCA / PALB2 status unknown — the pathway gates entirely on this result
Platinum induction has not occurred — POLO eligibility requires it as a prerequisite
MDS / AML risk on prolonged PARP exposure is the long-tail signal to monitor at year 2 and beyond

picks.intervention_label: ELI-002 7P amphiphile mKRAS peptide vaccine on NCT05726864
picks.rationale: The cleanest safety readout in the dossier, and the newer vaccine entries in this re-run do not beat it. AMPLIFY-201 (n=25, ELI-002 2P, G12D + G12R panel) reported zero DLTs through dose-escalation and no G3+ vaccine-attributed events, with injection-site reactions as the dominant AE class; the final 2025 report held that tolerability at 19.7-month median follow-up. The 7P successor carries the same amphiphile-peptide chemistry across seven KRAS variants including G12R. What separates this from the mKRASvax + dual-checkpoint entry that also appeared in the re-run is the toxicity ceiling: mKRASvax pairs a peptide vaccine with dual checkpoint blockade and logged G3 immune-related events — pneumonitis, adrenal insufficiency, myalgias, arthralgias — in 2/12 patients (17%), whereas ELI-002 as a bare vaccine adds no overlapping toxicity. The disqualifier stays the same: the trial enrolls MRD-positive resected disease, and this patient has overt recurrent disease outside that window unless a curative-intent salvage resection becomes feasible. Registry status is active-not-recruiting, which narrows access further.
primary_concerns: Overt-recurrent disease falls outside the MRD-positive enrollment window — eligibility is the gate, not safety
Active not recruiting per registry — access is the bottleneck
Vaccine effect needs immune competence and a 2-3 month T-cell expansion window; not a bridge for fast-progressing disease

picks.intervention_label: rucaparib 600 mg PO BID maintenance — contingent on germline or somatic BRCA1/2 or PALB2
picks.rationale: PARP-class backup to olaparib that widens the biomarker net to somatic BRCA and PALB2. Reiss 2021 phase 2 (n=46) reported mPFS 13.1 mo, mOS 23.5 mo, and ORR 41.7% in the measurable-disease subset, with no new safety signals at extended follow-up. The AE profile tracks the olaparib registrational data — anemia 74% any-grade / 22% G3+, nausea 48%, ALT elevation 47%, fatigue 45%, thrombocytopenia 39% — all under the same NCCN management framework, with one AE-driven withdrawal for G3 fatigue. Ranked below olaparib because the evidence is phase 2 single-arm rather than RCT, but the toxicity ceiling is the same well-characterized PARP class with the same MDS/AML long-tail. Same gating logic applies: germline or somatic HRD hit plus platinum induction before this is operative.
primary_concerns: Phase 2 single-arm rather than phase 3 RCT
Same germline / somatic HRD and platinum-exposure gates as olaparib
Anemia at 22% G3+ and the PARP-class MDS / AML risk on prolonged exposure

picks.intervention_label: ulixertinib (ERK1/2i) + palbociclib (CDK4/6i) on NCT03454035
picks.rationale: The one on-axis combination in the re-run that hits two of the patient's features — ERK blockade downstream of KRAS G12R and CDK4/6 inhibition for CDKN2A loss and CCND3 — while carrying a published, if abstract-level, toxicity table. Raybould/McRee ASCO 2021 (n=26; 9 PDAC) reported no G3/4/5 treatment-related deaths, with the G3 events named: decreased WBC, decreased lymphocytes, anemia, and fatigue. Common all-grade TRAEs were fatigue 70%, rash 62%, nausea 54%, with laboratory cytopenias frequent (lymphocytes down 77%, WBC down 73%, anemia 65%). Both component classes have management algorithms — the MAPK-inhibitor rash/GI ladder for ulixertinib, dose-hold-and-G-CSF cytopenia management for palbociclib — which is why this outranks the pan-KRAS/pan-RAS agents (JYP0015, JAB-23E73, KST-6051) that have no per-term G3+ AE distribution at all. What keeps it at rank 5 and low confidence rather than higher: the two toxicity axes overlap — MAPK-inhibitor GI/mucosal toxicity stacked on CDK4/6 cytopenias is synergistic myelosuppression not characterized in a dedicated combination-safety publication — and the pancreatic signal was 2 SD, not response. I will not rank it above the characterized-toxicity, gated options for a modest efficacy return.
primary_concerns: Overlapping myelosuppression (CDK4/6 cytopenias plus MAPK-inhibitor GI toxicity) not characterized in a dedicated PDAC combination-safety publication
Efficacy readout is stable disease in the pancreatic subset, not objective response; abstract-only with per-term G3 rates untabulated
G12R-specific organoid data absent from the supporting Knudsen 2023 synergy work; the lower baseline ERK flux of G12R is an open variable for an ERK-directed combination

notes: Re-run over the full current option set including the 6 new on-axis interventions. Targetable-feature scope rule applied; dropped the SoC chemo rows (FOLFIRINOX, gem/nab, NALIRIFOX, nal-IRI/5FU) per the considered_excluded tags — the treating team's call, not Libby's. On the three new pan-KRAS/pan-RAS agents: JYP0015/ERAS-0015 has an efficacy signal (PDAC uORR 40-42%, 14/14 with >=75% ctDNA reduction) but the source is a 27 Apr 2026 press release with no per-term G3+ AE rates and no peer-reviewed publication — that specific missing datum, the grade-resolved AE distribution, is what disqualifies it on the conservative axis despite a striking signal. JAB-23E73 (tier 5, empty toxicities, only a qualitative 'early antitumor activity' mention) and KST-6051/FALCON (tier 5, first patient dosed Apr 2026, no readout) have no clinical safety data at all and cannot be ranked. On the two new vaccine entries: mKRASvax + dual checkpoint logged G3 immune-related events (pneumonitis, adrenal insufficiency, myalgias, arthralgias) in 2/12 (17%) and the enrollable NCT06411691 is TPS-only with no efficacy readout — the added checkpoint toxicity is why ELI-002 as a bare vaccine ranks ahead of it; ABO2102 is tier 5 with no clinical data and unconfirmed G12R panel inclusion. Ranked ulixertinib + palbociclib at 5 over the pan-RAS newcomers specifically because it carries a named G3 AE table and per-class management algorithms, even abstract-level, which the pan-KRAS agents do not. The pan-RAS class still lacks 5-year safety follow-up, the conservative-default threshold; I pin rank 1 on 2-year data because the AE distribution is fully characterized and the alternatives are biomarker-mismatched chemo, gated PARP, or uncharacterized-toxicity early-phase agents. No hard toxicity-veto conflicts — preferences.json lists no formal vetoes. Round 2 watch-items: any pick layering RMC-6236 or a pan-RAS agent onto chemo without dedicated PDAC combination-safety data draws qualified dissent on toxicity; any checkpoint-combination vaccine pick (mKRASvax, ABO2102 + PD-1) draws qualified on toxicity citing the 17% G3 irAE rate; any pick of JYP0015/JAB-23E73/KST-6051 as rank 1-2 draws dissent on evidence_quality naming the absent grade-resolved AE distribution as the specific missing datum.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985, or expanded access if a slot is unavailable
picks.rationale: Still the only indication-matched, on-axis efficacy in this dossier that has cleared peer review, and even here the ceiling is ROBINS-I Moderate. Wolpin's NEJM 2026 report gives ORR 35%, mPFS 8.5 mo, mOS 13.1 mo in 2L RAS G12 PDAC at 300 mg, but that headline rests on n=26 pooled across G12 alleles with no G12R-resolved breakdown published, and the field is reading G12X as one estimand until the phase 3 lands. RASolute 302 (NCT06625320) is active-not-recruiting with no OS on file, so the registrational number that would actually settle this does not yet exist. Preclinical activity in G12R lines is consistent across Holderfield and Jiang, and Singhi's lower-ERK-flux G12R phenotype is a plausible reason the window might be wider here rather than narrower, but that is a hypothesis, not a result. It ranks first because everything below it is either double-gated or pre-data, not because the evidence is strong on its own terms.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I D1 confounding: single-arm open-label phase 1/2, sponsor analysis, no concurrent comparator
ROBINS-I D5/D6 outcome ascertainment: open-label ORR with no independent blinded review described in the available report
ROBINS-I D7 selective reporting: no G12R-specific subgroup ORR; the G12 pool masks the allele-resolved estimand the patient actually needs
Power: n=26 in the 2L RAS G12 arm at 300 mg cannot estimate a G12R-only effect with usable precision
Cross-allele extrapolation guard: the sotorasib and adagrasib PDAC readouts are G12C and do not transpose onto GTP-loaded G12R (Hobbs 2020)
Registrational confirmation pending: RASolute 302 OS is not reported

picks.intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after a platinum induction, contingent on a germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 hit
picks.rationale: The one RCT in the dossier that meets my bar on its own design: POLO is randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, RoB2:Low, with a pre-specified PFS primary met at HR 0.53 (95% CI 0.35-0.82, p=0.004). What keeps it at rank 2 rather than rank 1 is that the patient cannot enter it today. There is no germline result on file, and adjuvant FOLFIRI is irinotecan-based, so the patient is platinum-naive and the POLO entry condition (no progression after at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum) is not met. I also want the board to hold the endpoint honestly: POLO's interim OS HR was 0.91 and did not separate, so the PFS win has not carried through to survival even in the registrational population. Reiss's rucaparib data widen the eligible genotypes to somatic BRCA and PALB2 but that is single-arm n=42 with a 6-month PFS-rate primary, so it supports the class without clearing an RCT bar.
primary_concerns: Biomarker gate open: no germline BRCA1/2/PALB2 result; the germline-panel workup row is rate-limiting
Sequence gate open: patient is platinum-naive, so the POLO induction precondition is unmet
Endpoint hierarchy: POLO interim OS HR 0.91, no separation; PFS has not converted to OS
Rucaparib support (Reiss 2021) is single-arm n=42 with a PFS-rate primary, not RCT-grade

picks.intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
picks.rationale: This is the flashiest new number in the dossier and the one I most want to caveat. The PDAC unconfirmed ORR of 40% (n=20 at 16-32 mg) and 42% (n=12 at the RDE), plus 14/14 patients with at least 75% ctDNA reduction, come from an Erasca topline press release dated April 2026 with no abstract and no peer-reviewed paper. Responses are unconfirmed at a 14-week cutoff, per-term grade-3+ AE rates are undisclosed, and G12R is not reported separately, so allele-level confidence is lower than the pooled G12X figure suggests. Press-release efficacy is not evidence I can weight against the NEJM anchor above it, however good the mechanism story looks. It sits at rank 3 as a second on-axis pan-RAS option worth an enrollment call, not because the 40% is confirmed.
primary_concerns: Press-release maturity: no peer review, no abstract; the 40-42% ORR is unconfirmed at a 14-week cutoff
Selective/incomplete reporting: per-term grade-3+ AE rates not disclosed in the release
Allele resolution: G12R folded into the G12X gate and not reported on its own; the patient's minority allele is an indirect match through the pan-RAS mechanism
Single-arm dose-escalation, small n (20 PDAC), no comparator, no durability data

picks.intervention_label: pan-KRAS phase 1 with explicit G12R eligibility: PF-07934040 (NCT06447662) or ASP5834 (NCT07094204), with JAB-23E73 (NCT06959615) and KST-6051 / FALCON (NCT07458347) as further options
picks.rationale: A cluster of first-in-human pan-KRAS programs that name G12R in eligibility rather than hiding it in codon-12 language. None has an efficacy readout. PF-07934040 and ASP5834 are dose-finding with no responses reported; JAB-23E73 has only a qualitative 'early antitumor activity' mention with no numbers; KST-6051 dosed its first patient in April 2026 and has no data at all. I am grouping these as access redundancy behind the tri-complex class, offering different chemical mechanisms (oral pan-KRAS, IV degrader, ON/OFF switch-II binders) that might carve a distinct tolerability profile. This is positioning for a trial slot, not a ranking earned on evidence, and I would not represent any of them to the patient as having shown benefit.
primary_concerns: No efficacy readout on any of the four: dose-finding only
JAB-23E73 and KST-6051 disclosures are informal:high, tier 5; no numeric efficacy or per-term AE data exist yet
No published toxicity profile beyond protocol exclusions (grade 2+ neuropathy excluded from PF-07934040, a watch-item post-FOLFIRI)
PDAC-specific dose-level cohorts will be small and exploratory; confirm an open PDAC slot rather than trusting the global enrollment statement

picks.intervention_label: mutant-KRAS vaccine strategies (ELI-002 7P NCT05726864; mKRASvax + dual checkpoint NCT06411691; ABO2102 mRNA NCT06577532) — flagged, not endorsed
picks.rationale: I am ranking the vaccine axis last and mainly to document why it does not go higher. The strongest datum, AMPLIFY-201 (Wainberg 2025, Pant 2024), is a single-arm phase 1 n=25 at ROBINS-I:Serious, and its survival separation is a responder-stratified split by above- vs below-median T-cell expansion, which is exactly the kind of post-hoc immunogenicity subgroup I discount. The anchor for the enrollable mKRASvax trial is a resected-PDAC phase 1 (Huff 2026, n=12) with median DFS 6.35 mo and a biomarker primary; the trial itself, NCT06411691, is TPS-only with no efficacy and requires ECOG 0 plus prior metastatic FOLFIRINOX the patient has not had. Every vaccine row here is either MRD/adjuvant setting (line mismatch for overt-recurrent disease) or has unconfirmed G12R inclusion in its encoded panel. The ABO2102 mRNA class rests on a 2-patient G12V correspondence, a different allele. Mechanistically rational for an MSS, immune-cold tumor with no ICI route; clinically unproven in this setting.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I:Serious across the vaccine evidence: single-arm phase 1, small n, no comparator
Responder-stratified survival split (above/below-median T-cell expansion) is a post-hoc immunogenicity subgroup, not a pre-specified endpoint
Line/setting mismatch: AMPLIFY-201 and mKRASvax anchor are resected/adjuvant MRD; this patient is overt-recurrent, out of the enrollment window
Allele match unconfirmed: G12R inclusion in the ABO2102 mRNA panel is not stated in the registry; the G12V mRNA precedent is a 2-patient correspondence in a different allele
Trial-in-progress: NCT06411691 is TPS-only with no efficacy, requires ECOG 0 (patient is ECOG 1) and prior metastatic FOLFIRINOX (not received)

notes: Re-run over the expanded option set with six new on-axis trials. The evidence hierarchy has not moved as much as the trial count. The one indication-matched peer-reviewed efficacy signal is still daraxonrasib at ROBINS-I Moderate with a load-bearing 26-patient pooled-G12 subgroup and no G12R breakdown; the one RCT-grade design (POLO, RoB2:Low) is one the patient cannot enter without a germline hit and a platinum induction. The heavily promoted new datum, JYP0015/ERAS-0015 at PDAC uORR 40-42%, is a press release: unconfirmed, no peer review, per-term AE undisclosed, G12R not resolved, so it cannot be weighted against the NEJM anchor and lands at rank 3 on maturity grounds alone. JAB-23E73 and KST-6051 are pre-data first-in-human with informal:high risk-of-bias and no efficacy, so they are access-positioning, not evidence. On the vaccine axis: the mKRASvax anchor (Huff 2026, PMID 41667470) is a resected/adjuvant phase 1, and AMPLIFY-201's survival signal is a below-vs-above-median T-cell responder split, a subgroup analysis I discount; the enrollable NCT06411691 is TPS-only and gates on ECOG 0 and prior metastatic FOLFIRINOX this patient lacks, so the setting mismatch is real for a recurrent patient. Downweighted and not ranked: palbociclib monotherapy (NCI-MATCH Z1C, O'Hara 2025, ORR 4% — an actively negative basket, though CDKN2A-loss-enriched arms have not read out); ulixertinib+palbociclib (Raybould ASCO 2021 abstract-only, n=26, PDAC signal was stable disease not response, ROBINS-I:Serious); avutometinib+defactinib RAMP 205 (83% ORR at dose level 1 is n=6, ASCO abstract, ROBINS-I:Serious — signal-finding); PaTcH trametinib+HCQ terminated for futility, which downweights the MEK+autophagy basket until it generates its own data. Foreclosed cleanly: tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab (MSS, TMB 4.1; KEYNOTE-158 is MSI-H only) and dual-ICI-plus-chemo (Renouf PA.7, RoB2:Low, p=0.72). I have not read the primary reports behind the JYP0015 press release or the JAB-23E73/KST-6051 disclosures, so those bias assessments rest on the abstracts and topline text, not the underlying data. From a strict RCT-grade stance this case still has no comfortable answer, but I am not abstaining: one peer-reviewed indication-matched signal and one clean RCT the patient can work toward is enough to rank rather than decline.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) via trial or FDA Expanded Access (RMC-6236-001 NCT05379985, RMC-GI-102 NCT06445062; RASolute 302 NCT06625320 is the registrational readout)
picks.rationale: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 makes clinical-trial enrollment the preferred route for recurrent disease with an actionable alteration, and a confirmed KRAS G12R points straight at the pan-RAS(ON) class. The evidence base moved since the prior run: RASolute 302 read out positive (mOS 13.2 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.40, ITT), which sits on top of the Wolpin NEJM 2026 phase 1/2 numbers (ORR 35%, mPFS 8.5, mOS 13.1 in 2L RAS G12 at 300 mg), and the FDA authorized an Expanded Access Program in May 2026. It is still not an NCCN evidence-category regimen for PDAC and ESMO has not scored it, so the guideline fit is the trial-enrollment principle plus a now-positive phase 3 rather than a category 1 or 2A drug listing.
primary_concerns: Not an NCCN-listed regimen; the guideline case rests on the trial-enrollment principle plus the RASolute 302 phase-3 readout and the FDA Expanded Access route, not a category 1/2A drug endorsement.
G12R sits inside the pooled G12X estimand; no allele-resolved subgroup ORR has been published, so the read-across to this specific allele carries residual uncertainty.
RASolute 302 is active not recruiting, so the practical routes are RMC-GI-102 (NCT06445062), RMC-6236-001 (NCT05379985), or the Expanded Access Program rather than the registrational trial.

picks.intervention_label: olaparib maintenance after platinum induction, gated on the germline BRCA1/2 panel (POLO regimen)
picks.rationale: This is the only genuine category-1 drug-level endorsement anywhere on the menu for this patient: NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 lists olaparib maintenance as category 1 for germline BRCA1/2-mutant metastatic PDAC after at least 16 weeks of first-line platinum without progression, and it recommends germline testing for every PDAC patient regardless of family history. POLO (Golan 2019 NEJM, PFS HR 0.53) is the RCT behind the FDA approval and ESMO endorses the same indication. Two gates sit in front of it here, and both are real: germline status is not on file, and the patient is platinum-naive after irinotecan-based FOLFIRI, so a platinum induction would have to come first and hold. I rank it second anyway because when the guideline actually speaks at category 1, that outweighs a deeper but pre-approval trial option.
primary_concerns: Germline status is unknown; the whole pathway is contingent on the panel returning a pathogenic BRCA1, BRCA2, or PALB2 variant. Order it now.

The patient is platinum-naive after FOLFIRI adjuvant, so a NALIRIFOX or FOLFIRINOX induction (treating team's call, outside Libby's scope) would need to control disease for 16+ weeks before the POLO indication opens.
Rucaparib (Reiss 2021 JCO) covers somatic BRCA and PALB2 but is not category 1 in NCCN PDAC, so it is a fallback rather than an equivalent.

picks.intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
picks.rationale: New on-axis trial since the prior run, and it is the strongest of the six new options on data. The phase 1 press release reports unconfirmed PDAC ORR of 40-42% at the RDE with 14/14 KRAS G12X patients showing at least 75% ctDNA reduction, and eligibility turns on a RAS mutation rather than an allele list, so G12R is covered. Same guideline logic as daraxonrasib: no NCCN category, no ESMO MCBS score, so it aligns through the trial-enrollment principle in v2.2026. It ranks below daraxonrasib because the evidence is a topline release rather than a peer-reviewed phase 3, but it is a legitimate same-mechanism backup if RAS(ON) access is blocked.
primary_concerns: Efficacy is from an April 2026 topline release with no peer-reviewed publication; confirmed responses and per-term grade 3+ AE rates are not available.
G12R is not reported separately; the 40-42% is pooled across G12X and the specific-allele read-across is unproven.
Not NCCN-listed or ESMO-scored for PDAC; confirm an open PDAC slot at a participating site before banking on it.

picks.intervention_label: PF-07934040 pan-KRAS small molecule on NCT06447662
picks.rationale: Pfizer's pan-KRAS program names G12R in its written eligibility criteria, which is unusual among the first-in-human pan-KRAS agents and makes it a clean third pan-RAS-axis backup after daraxonrasib and ERAS-0015. The guideline fit is again the NCCN v2.2026 trial-enrollment principle, not a drug-level listing; ESMO has not scored the class. The phase 1 is recruiting with a 2L+ PDAC monotherapy cohort (Part 2a A1) that matches the post-FOLFIRI setting and a separate 1L gem/nab combination arm.
primary_concerns: Phase 1 with no mature efficacy published; RP2D in the PDAC cohort is still being set.
Grade 2+ sensory neuropathy is an exclusion; prior FOLFIRI is a watch-item, though irinotecan-based regimens are usually neuropathy-sparing.
Not NCCN-listed or ESMO-scored; ranks below the two pan-RAS options only because the clinical-data depth is thinner still.

picks.intervention_label: anvumetostat (AMG 193) PRMT5 inhibitor on MTAPESTRY-103 (NCT06360354), gated on MTAP co-deletion
picks.rationale: CDKN2A and MTAP are neighbors on 9p21 and co-deleted in roughly 80-90% of CDKN2A homozygous deletions, and the MTA-cooperative PRMT5 class (Mavrakis 2016 and Kryukov 2016 Science; Smith 2023 Cancer Discovery for MRTX1719) is the synthetic-lethal axis tied to this patient's CDKN2A loss. NCT06360354 carries a daraxonrasib combination arm that would cover both the KRAS G12R and the CDKN2A-loss / MTAP-deletion features in one trial. NCCN v2.2026 has no MTAP-deletion line item, so trial enrollment is once more the guideline-aligned route; the pick also depends on an MTAP reflex test that has not yet been run.
primary_concerns: MTAP co-deletion is unconfirmed for this patient; the rationale collapses if MTAP is retained. Add the MTAP IHC/NGS reflex.
MTA-cooperative PRMT5 inhibitors are early-phase across every indication; PDAC-specific efficacy is not published.
No NCCN category for this class in PDAC; the pick rides on biomarker-plus-trial alignment, not a drug-level endorsement.

notes: Re-run over the full current option set, including the six new on-axis interventions from the trial re-screen. Where the new options landed: JYP0015/ERAS-0015 (NCT06895031) earned rank 3 on its topline PDAC ORR 40-42% and ctDNA data. The two pan-KRAS ON/OFF trials, JAB-23E73 (NCT06959615) and KST-6051/FALCON (NCT07458347), name G12R but carry no clinical efficacy yet (first patient dosed April 2026 for FALCON), so they sit below PF-07934040 as trial-enrollment-principle options without a data anchor. The two KRAS-vaccine-plus-checkpoint trials, ABO2102 mRNA vaccine +/- toripalimab (NCT06577532) and mKRASvax + balstilimab/botensilimab (NCT06411691), are biologically rational in an MSS immune-cold tumor where ICI monotherapy is foreclosed, but neither confirms G12R is in its encoded panel, NCT06411691 requires 4-6 months of prior metastatic first-line chemo and ECOG 0 that this ECOG-1 post-adjuvant patient does not meet, and neither has efficacy data; they are trial-enrollment options a rung below the pan-RAS axis. Ulixertinib + palbociclib (NCT03454035) hits both the KRAS-downstream ERK and CDKN2A/CCND3 axes and admits PDAC by histology, but it is an off-label off-guideline combination on a single-arm phase 1, so it does not displace the better-anchored picks. Standard-of-care chemotherapy (FOLFIRINOX, NALIRIFOX, gem/nab, nal-IRI/5FU) is category 1/2A in NCCN Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma v2.2026 for recurrent disease but is out of Libby's targetable-feature scope and is the treating team's call. Single-agent CDK4/6 inhibition is not guideline-listed for PDAC and the NCI-MATCH Z1C palbociclib basket (O'Hara 2025 CCR, ORR 4%) reads negative. ICI is foreclosed by MSS plus TMB 4.1 against the FDA tumor-agnostic pembrolizumab thresholds (Marabelle 2020 JCO; Renouf 2022 PA.7 negative for biomarker-agnostic ICI on chemo). Four of five picks ride on the NCCN trial-enrollment principle rather than a drug-level category, with olaparib the lone category-1 option and only after two gating workups. That is the honest guideline picture for an MSS, sub-TMB-threshold, KRAS G12R recurrent PDAC where the actionable menu is dominated by pre-approval agents.

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) monotherapy on NCT05379985
picks.rationale: This is still the pick that gives the patient what they asked for with the least hand-waving. Recruiting trial, oral once daily, and the Wolpin NEJM 2026 cohort at 300 mg in 2L RAS G12 PDAC put up ORR 35%, mPFS 8.5 mo, mOS 13.1 mo. G12R sits inside the pooled G12X estimand rather than a named subgroup, so I have to be straight that the allele-specific number is not published — but it is the best clinical efficacy anyone has shown on this axis, and with a 0.80 efficacy weight and treat-to-remission as the stated goal, that is what the preference set rewards. Grade 3+ TRAEs near 30%, rash and GI as the class effects, land well within what a patient carrying no toxicity vetoes has consented to. The only screening step is the orthogonal NGS or ctDNA G12R confirmation, which is already scoped.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: prefers_trials (recruiting), efficacy-lean weight, treat-to-remission framing, no toxicity veto to trip
In tension: G12R-specific ORR is not broken out — the read rests on the pooled G12X number pending phase 3
Operational: baseline G12R confirmation on orthogonal NGS / ctDNA is the entry gate

picks.intervention_label: JYP0015 / ERAS-0015 pan-RAS molecular glue on NCT06895031
picks.rationale: New on the board and it earns a high slot on the patient's own terms. It is a cyclophilin-A pan-RAS molecular glue that engages GTP-bound KRAS across G12X, PDAC is a named recruiting cohort, oral once daily, and the April 2026 topline read an unconfirmed PDAC ORR of 40-42% with 14 of 14 KRAS G12X patients dropping ctDNA at least 75% and a third clearing to zero. That is a second independent pan-RAS signal in the same ORR range as daraxonrasib, which is exactly the kind of corroboration a remission-seeking patient should want before committing to a class. I will not oversell it: this is a press release, not a peer-reviewed paper, per-term grade-3 rates are not out, and G12R is covered under the G12X gate rather than reported on its own — so predictive confidence for this specific allele is lower than the pooled figure suggests. Confirm an open PDAC slot at a participating site.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: prefers_trials (recruiting), efficacy-lean weight, oral, treat-to-remission framing
In tension: efficacy is an unpublished topline; no per-term safety table yet and G12R is pooled inside G12X
Operational: confirm an active PDAC cohort slot and baseline G12R confirmation

picks.intervention_label: daraxonrasib + mFOLFIRINOX or gem/nab on NCT06445062 (RMC-GI-102)
picks.rationale: If treat to remission is the load-bearing phrase in preferences.json, this is the route that takes it at face value. The patient had adjuvant FOLFIRI only, so they are oxaliplatin-naive and an mFOLFIRINOX arm is biologically on the table, and the RAMP-205 dose-level-1 read of 5/6 confirmed PRs on a chemo-plus-targeted backbone shows the depth of response combination intensification can reach in RAS-mutant PDAC. Stacking pan-RAS toxicity (rash, GI) on chemo toxicity (cytopenia, neuropathy) is a real cost, and the free text tells me the patient will take that trade — accepts high-risk-high-reward. The gate is operational: confirm the PDAC subprotocol is open at the referral site, and let residual neuropathy from prior FOLFIRI steer the backbone toward gem/nab if needed.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: prefers_trials, efficacy-lean weight, high-risk-high-reward explicitly invited
Operational: PDAC arm openness varies by site — sponsor / treating-team confirmation needed
In tension: prior FOLFIRI may push the backbone to gem/nab over mFOLFIRINOX depending on residual neuropathy

picks.intervention_label: KST-6051 / FALCON pan-KRAS (ON/OFF) inhibitor on NCT07458347
picks.rationale: A clean backup on the primary KRAS axis for when the daraxonrasib and JYP0015 slots are full. It is an oral Switch-II-pocket pan-KRAS inhibitor active against ON and OFF states, PDAC is a named tumor type, the 2L+ line matches the post-adjuvant setting, and eligibility turns on a documented KRAS mutation with no allele-restricting list, so G12R qualifies without argument. Prior RAS inhibitor is an exclusion, which is intact for this RAS-inhibitor-naive patient. The honest limit is maturity: first patient dosed April 2026, no efficacy or safety readout exists, so this rides entirely on the pan-RAS class rationale and G12R's biology sitting in the active-state window. Early-phase slots will be scarce.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: prefers_trials (recruiting), oral, PDAC named, G12R covered by the KRAS-mutation gate
In tension: no clinical efficacy or safety data — pure class extrapolation on an early dose-escalation
Operational: dose-escalation slots are limited this early in the trial

picks.intervention_label: JAB-23E73 pan-KRAS (ON/OFF) inhibitor on NCT06959615
picks.rationale: A second pan-KRAS ON/OFF entry to keep on the list because redundancy on the patient's primary axis is a feature, not padding — if one early-phase trial has no slot, the next one might. Its preclinical profile names G12R among the covered G12X alleles, it spares HRAS/NRAS, and the broad KRAS-alteration eligibility admits this patient; prior RAS-targeting therapy is excluded, which is intact here. Two caveats I will not bury: the trial enrolls any advanced solid tumor rather than naming PDAC, so I would confirm a pancreatic slot rather than assume one, and the only clinical disclosure so far is a qualitative early-antitumor-activity mention with no numbers. Below KST-6051 only because that trial names PDAC explicitly.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: prefers_trials (recruiting), oral, G12R named among covered alleles, RAS-inhibitor-naive
In tension: basket enrolls any solid tumor — PDAC slot not guaranteed; no numeric efficacy or per-term safety yet
Operational: confirm a PDAC slot at a participating site

picks.intervention_label: ulixertinib (ERK1/2i) + palbociclib (CDK4/6i) on NCT03454035
picks.rationale: The one ranked option that hits two of the patient's features in a single regimen — ulixertinib blocks ERK downstream of KRAS G12R and palbociclib targets the CDK4/6 dependency created by CDKN2A loss and CCND3 alteration. The PDAC expansion admits pancreatic cancer by histology after at least one prior line, so G12R is not a gate and the 2L+ line and ECOG 1 both fit; it is recruiting and oral. I am putting it last for a reason the patient deserves stated plainly: the published pancreatic signal (Raybould ASCO 2021) was stable disease, not response, and the Knudsen 2023 organoid synergy that motivates it was worked out mostly in G12D/G12V lines while G12R runs a lower baseline ERK flux (Singhi 2025), so the combination logic is sound but the depth-of-response case is thinner than the pan-RAS arms above. For a remission-seeking patient, dual-feature coverage is worth keeping on the table even at a modest efficacy prior.
primary_concerns: Fully satisfied: prefers_trials (recruiting), oral, single regimen covering KRAS + CDKN2A/CCND3 axes, G12R not an eligibility barrier
In tension: best published PDAC signal is stable disease, not objective response — lower efficacy prior than the pan-RAS options
In tension: synergy data are G12D/G12V-dominant; G12R's lower ERK flux is an open variable

notes: Re-run over the full current option set after the 6 new on-axis trials landed. Preferences remain unusually permissive — no toxicity vetoes, no modality constraints, efficacy_toxicity_weight 0.80, treat-to-remission goal, accepts high-risk-high-reward, prefers trials — so nothing on the board trips a preference filter and the ranking is free to bias toward deepest-response options on the patient's primary KRAS axis. The new pan-RAS glue JYP0015 is the biggest mover: it jumps to rank 2 on a second independent 40%-range PDAC ORR signal plus striking ctDNA clearance, tempered only because the data are a press release and G12R is pooled inside G12X. Daraxonrasib monotherapy holds rank 1 on the strength of an actual NEJM publication. The two pan-KRAS ON/OFF trials (KST-6051, JAB-23E73) are ranked but flagged low-confidence — mechanism-clean and G12R-eligible, no efficacy yet. ulixertinib+palbociclib is the deliberate dual-feature keeper at rank 6. Held off the ranked list: the KRAS vaccine routes (ABO2102 on NCT06577532, mKRASvax+dual-checkpoint on NCT06411691) are mechanism-attractive for an MSS/low-TMB tumor where checkpoint monotherapy is dead, but ABO2102's G12R panel inclusion is unconfirmed in the registry and the Hopkins mKRASvax cohort gates on ECOG 0 and 4-6 months of prior metastatic first-line chemo the patient has not had — both are eligibility mismatches, not preference conflicts, so I surface them as watch-items rather than picks. zoldonrasib+ivonescimab (NCT07397338) remains a high-ceiling immune-axis option but its primary indications are NSCLC/CRC and PDAC-cohort openness is unconfirmed. Olaparib (POLO, PMID 31157963) stays off the ranked list pending the germline panel and a platinum induction; if germline BRCA1/2 or PALB2 turns positive, the board should revisit. Standard-of-care chemo is out of scope under the targetable-feature rule and is the treating team's call.
